title: Assessing persister awakening dynamics following antibiotic treatment in E. coli
protocol: Inoculate the preculture in a glass tube containing 5 mL LB medium.
Incubate the culture at 37°C at 200 rpm for 20–24 hours.
Dilute the preculture 100-fold in 5 mL LB medium.
Incubate the diluted culture at 37°C at 200 rpm for 16–18 hours.
Take 990 μL of the culture and add it to an empty, sterile glass tube.
Add 10 μL of the ofloxacin stock solution to achieve a concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Incubate the tube at 37°C at 200 rpm for 5 hours.
Prepare the LB agarose in the meantime.
Prepare the microscopy slide.
Remove the protection layer from the gene frame.
Stick the gene frame to a glass slide.
Take approximately 200 μL of heated LB-agarose.
Pipette the heated LB-agarose into the middle of the gene frame until it is completely filled.
Take a glass cover slip.
Gently press the cover slip on the gene frame without removing the protective layer, flattening the LB-agarose.
Let the LB-agarose pad dry for 2–5 hours at room temperature.
Ensure the microscope incubation chamber is at 37°C.
Pipette 100 μL of your sample into an Eppendorf tube after 5 hours of treatment with ofloxacin.
Centrifuge the cells at 3,000 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of pre-heated LB.
Gently remove the cover slip on top of the LB-agarose pad by sliding.
Take a scalpel and go over the inner border of the gene frame to prevent damage when removing the protective layer from the sticky blue border.
Add 2 μL of the washed culture in the middle of the LB-agarose pad.
Gently tap the side of the slide against the bench, spreading the culture.
Let the liquid evaporate completely for a couple of minutes.
Remove the protective layer from the sticky blue border of the gene frame.
Put a glass cover slip on top of the gene frame and gently press it.
Note down the time after setting up the LB-agarose pad.
Select XY positions that are not overcrowded with cells.
Avoid selecting positions near large clusters or "walls" of cells.
Choose positions containing varying numbers of cells for analysis.
Optimize the number of XY positions based on the persister fraction, typically around 25 for a 1% fraction.
Adjust the number of XY positions if the persister fraction is higher, possibly reducing to about 15.
Ensure the interval between time points is 15–20 minutes to accommodate the total duration of 18 hours.
Identify the persister cells.
Follow E. coli BW25113 after ofloxacin treatment.
Define persister cells as those capable of dividing more than four times (n > 4).
Observe formation of micro-colonies in time-lapse microscopy data.
Analyze persister awakening kinetics.
Measure the length of the persister cell over time.
Determine the awakening lag from the growth curve.
Determine when cell division occurs using a consistent method.
Calculate the time between awakening lag and cell division for each cell.
Analyze growth kinetics of sensitive cells as they elongate.
Randomly select sensitive cells from frames containing persister cells.
Follow the length of sensitive cells over at least 180 minutes post-antibiotic treatment.
Determine the awakening lag for sensitive cells by measuring time to double initial size.
